newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus protests at Turkish warship docking.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus protests at Turkish warship docking.

text.p: The Cyprus government on Tuesday said it would protest to the United Nations against the arrival of six Turkish warships and three submarines in northern Cyprus for naval exercises.

The Greek Cypriot-led government said the protest would also concern the infringement of the Nicosia flight information region, an area administered by the Cyprus civil aviation department, by 16 Turkish F-16s on Sunday and Monday.
"A relevant protest will be made to the United Nations," government spokesman Manolis Christofides said.
Three Turkish gunboats and one submarine anchored at the northern Kyrenia harbour, and three frigates and two submarines docked at the eastern port of Famagusta on Monday.
The flotilla is to depart on June 20, Turkish Cypriot agency TAK reported.

Cyprus has been divided since Turkey invaded in 1974 after a short-lived coup in Nicosia backed by the military junta then ruling Greece. A self-declared Turkish Cypriot state in the north is recognised only by Turkey.

The leaders of the island's Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities are due to embark on a new round of United Nations-sponsored direct talks in New York on July 9 in an attempt to bridge differences between the two sides.
